'''Bennet Evan Miller''' (born 24 February 1966) is an English comedian, actor, and author. He rose to fame as a member of the comedy duo [[Armstrong and Miller]], with fellow comedian [[Alexander Armstrong]]. His credits include ''[[Armstrong and Miller (TV series)|Armstrong and Miller]]'' (1997-2001), ''[[The Parole Officer]]'' (2001), ''[[Johnny English]]'' (2003), ''[[The Prince and Me]]'' (2004), ''[[The Worst Week of My Life]]'' (2005), ''[[Saxondale]]'' (2006), ''[[Primeval (TV series)|Primeval]]'' (2007-2011), ''[[Razzle Dazzle: A Journey into Dance]]'' (2007), ''[[Huge (film)|Huge]]'' (2010), ''[[Death in Paradise]]'' (2011–2014), ''[[Molly Moon and the Incredible Book of Hypnotism]]'' (2012), ''[[What We Did on Our Holiday]]''  (2014), ''[[Horrible Histories (2015 TV series)#Series 6 .282015.29|Horrible Histories]]'' (2015), ''[[It's Not Rocket Science (TV series)|It's Not Rocket Science]]'' (2015), ''[[Doctor Who]]'' - "[[Robot of Sherwood|episode: Robot of Sherwood]]" (2016),  ''[[I Want My Wife Back]]'' (2016), ''[[Ballot Monkeys]]'' (2016), ''[[Johnny English Strikes Again]]'' (2018), ''[[Upstart Crow]]'' (2018), ''[[Sticks and Stones (TV series)|Sticks and Stones]]'' (2019), ''[[Bridgerton]]'' (2020), ''[[Professor T. (British TV series)|Professor T.]]'' (2021–2026), and ''[[Austin (TV series)|Austin]]'' (2024).

==Early life and education ==
Bennet Evan Miller's parents were teachers. His father taught [[American literature]] at the [[City of Birmingham Polytechnic]]. His mother was from [[Neath]], Wales.<ref name=Bevan2015 /> His paternal grandfather was a tailor in the [[East End of London]], while his paternal great-grandmother taught English at [[South Cheshire College]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p038xdzt |title=Ben Miller finds out an amazing fact, Series 10, Coming Home |first=Ben |last=Miller|website=BBC |access-date=16 May 2017 |date=23 November 2015|format =video, 2 mins }}</ref> He has two younger sisters.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2010/sep/11/ben-miller-family-values|title = Ben Miller: My family values |work=[[The Guardian]] |first=Caroline |last=Rees |date=10 September 2010}}</ref> He is a distant cousin of [[Abraham Lincoln]].<ref name=Bevan2015>{{Cite news |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/lifestyle/tv/ben-miller-one-ancestors-welsh-10513886 |first=Nathan |last=Bevan |title=Ben Miller - my ancestors the Welsh war hero and the US president |work=Wales Online |date=27 November 2015}}</ref>

Miller was educated at [[Malbank School and Sixth Form College]] in [[Nantwich]] before studying [[Natural Sciences (Cambridge)|Natural Sciences]] at [[St Catharine's College, Cambridge]]. As an undergraduate, he participated in theatre with his girlfriend, actress [[Rachel Weisz]].<ref name="Thismuch">[https://www.theguardian.com/stage/2008/feb/24/comedy.television1 This much I know: Ben Miller], ''The Observer'', 24 February 2008</ref> He remained at Cambridge to undertake a [[PhD]] in [[solid state physics]], with the title of his proposed thesis being "Novel quantum effects in low-temperature [[Quantum dot|quasi-zero-dimensional]] [[Mesoscopic scale|mesoscopic]] electron systems".<ref>{{Cite journal |url=http://www.iop.org/careers/working-life/profiles/page_65895.html|title=Once a physicist: Ben Miller|publisher=Institute of Physics|journal=Physics World|volume=28|issue=7|pages=55|access-date=13 March 2016|bibcode=2015PhyW...28g..55.|year=2015|doi=10.1088/2058-7058/28/7/53|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="RocketScience">{{cite book |last=Miller |first=Ben |author-link=Ben Miller |year=2012 |title=It's Not Rocket Science}}</ref><ref name="QI">{{cite episode |title=The Future |series=[[QI]] |station=[[BBC One]] |airdate= 20 February 2009}}</ref> 

He abandoned his thesis to pursue a career in comedy.<ref name="RocketScience" /> His interest in comedy began when a friend asked him to help chauffeur the judges of the [[National Student Drama Festival]], which was being held that year in Cambridge.<ref name="newsau1">{{cite news |url=http://www.news.com.au/couriermail/story/0,23739,21317809-5003420,00.html |title=Ben dazzles 'em |website=news.com.au |date=4 March 2007 |access-date=16 October 2007 |archive-date=7 September 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120907035049/http://www.couriermail.com.au/entertainment/movies/ben-dazzles-em/story-e6freqex-1111113091904 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Having finished his degree, he joined the [[Footlights]] in 1989 and worked with [[Andy Parsons]], [[David Wolstencroft]] and [[Sue Perkins]] before he directed a revue.<ref>{{cite news|title=The Cambridge Footlights: First steps into comedy |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/comedy/features/the-cambridge-footlights-first-steps-in-comedy-1517691.html|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|date=28 January 2009}}</ref>

==Career==
Miller moved to London to pursue a career in comedy.<ref name="BBCPOAM">{{cite web|title= The Armstrong & Miller Show – Armstrong and Miller |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/pressoffice/pressreleases/stories/2007/10_october/12/armstrong_biog.shtml |work=BBC Press Office |date=12 October 2007}}</ref> He was introduced to fellow Cambridge graduate [[Alexander Armstrong (comedian)|Alexander Armstrong]] in 1992, at the TBA Sketch Comedy Group, a comedy club which ran at the [[Gate Theatre Studio]], [[Notting Hill]] throughout the 1990s. They performed their first full-length show together at the [[Edinburgh Fringe]] in 1994, and returned when they were nominated for the [[Perrier Comedy Award]] 1996.<ref name="perrier">{{cite web|title= Edinburgh Comedy Awards: 1996 Perrier Comedy Awards |url= https://www.comedy.co.uk/awards/directory/edinburgh-comedy-awards/1996/ |work= comedy.co.uk |access-date= 22 March 2026}}</ref>

Their success resulted in the commission of the television series ''[[Armstrong and Miller (TV series)|Armstrong and Miller]]'',<ref name="tv">{{cite web|title= Ben Miller Credits |url= https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/ben-miller/credits/3030396491/ |work= tvguide.com |access-date= 22 March 2026}}</ref> which ran for four series from 1997 to 2001 – one on the [[Paramount Comedy Channel]] and three on [[Channel 4]]. In 1998, the duo also had their own [[Armstrong and Miller (radio show)|radio show]] with the same name on [[BBC Radio 4]], which featured many of the sketches and characters from their TV series. After a six-year break,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://twitter.com/bennylicious/status/3741389386 |title=Ben Miller Twitter post on 2nd series |publisher=Twitter |date=3 September 2009 |access-date=3 September 2009}}</ref> the show was recommissioned for [[Hat Trick Productions]] as ''[[The Armstrong & Miller Show]]'' and three series have been produced.<ref name="femalefirst1">{{cite web|url=http://www.femalefirst.co.uk/celebrity_interviews/Ben+Miller-254691.html |title=Ben Miller Interview |publisher=Femalefirst.co.uk |date=29 August 2012 |access-date=27 January 2019}}</ref> In 2008, they also had a second radio show, ''Children's Hour with Armstrong and Miller''.<ref name=BBCR4E1>{{cite web|title=Children's Hour with Armstrong and Miller|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00fqh9v/episodes/guide|work=Episode guide|publisher=BBC Radio 4 Extra|access-date=17 February 2014}}</ref>

Miller also started acting in films, starring in [[Steve Coogan]]'s first feature film, ''[[The Parole Officer]]'' (2001).<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/1484336.stm "Coogan's out on Parole"], BBC News, 10 August 2001</ref> In 2003 he played the role of Bough, sidekick to [[Rowan Atkinson]]'s title character, in the film ''[[Johnny English]]''.<ref name="tv"/> In 2004 he co-starred in the romantic comedy ''[[The Prince and Me]]''.<ref name="tv"/>

In 2004 and 2005, he starred alongside [[Sarah Alexander]] in two series of the [[BBC]] television series ''[[The Worst Week of My Life]]''.<ref name="tv"/><ref name="5Min">{{cite news |title=The 5-Minute Interview: Ben Miller |date=21 December 2005 |work=The Independent |via=[[FindArticles]] |url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qn4158/is_20051221/ai_n15942439 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081206163010/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qn4158/is_20051221/ai_n15942439 |archive-date=December 6, 2008 |url-status=usurped}}</ref><ref name="HWM1">{{cite news |title=HOW WE MET: Sarah Alexander & Ben Miller |date=7 March 2004 |work=[[The Independent on Sunday]] |via=[[FindArticles]] |url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qn4159/is_20040307/ai_n12751087/print |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081011034715/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qn4159/is_20040307/ai_n12751087/print |archive-date=October 11, 2008 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> In 2006 he took part in a three-part Christmas special, ''The Worst Christmas of My Life''. He starred as [[James Peregrine Lester]] in ITV's sci-fi drama ''[[Primeval (TV series)|Primeval]]'' (2007),<ref name="tv"/> and as children's dance instructor Mr Jonathan in the Australian [[mockumentary]] film ''[[Razzle Dazzle: A Journey into Dance]]''.<ref name="newsau1" />

He and [[Alexander Armstrong (comedian)|Alexander Armstrong]] formed a production company named Toff Media in 2007. The company was dissolved in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TOFF MEDIA LIMITED overview - Find and update company information - GOV.UK |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/06150936 |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk |language=en}}</ref>

Miller provided the voice for the [[ITV Digital]] and later [[PG Tips]] [[Monkey (character)|Monkey]] in a popular series of television advertisements featuring [[Johnny Vegas]].<ref>{{cite press release|date=1 August 2007|title=Al and monkey bring back the monkey magic|url= http://www.unilever.co.uk/ourcompany/newsandmedia/pressreleases/2007/Al_and_monkey_magic.asp|url-status=dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20071125144503/http://www.unilever.co.uk/ourcompany/newsandmedia/pressreleases/2007/Al_and_monkey_magic.asp|archive-date=25 November 2007|publisher=Unilever Press Dept}}</ref> In 2008, he appeared as television producer Jonathan Pope in [[Tony Jordan]]'s series ''[[Moving Wallpaper]]'' on [[ITV1]] and starred in ''[[Thank God You're Here (British TV series)|Thank God You're Here]]''.<ref name="tv"/> 

In 2009, Miller appeared with [[Rob Brydon]] in an episode of ''[[QI]]'' (Series 6. 9).<ref name="tv"/> The two have often been mistaken for each other,<ref name="Thismuch" /><ref name="5Min" /> and as a joke they dressed in similar shirts for the episode and shared an on-screen kiss.<ref name="QI" /><ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00hq4mg#synopsis Series 6: Episode 9 of 12] ''BBC QI Broadcasts'' – Accessed 20 May 2010</ref>

In 2010, he made his directorial debut with the film ''[[Huge (film)|Huge]]''.<ref name="tv"/> In January 2011 he presented an episode of the BBC science series ''[[Horizon (British TV series)|Horizon]]''<ref name="tv"/> titled [[List of Horizon episodes#Series 47: 2010–2011|"What is One Degree?"]]. Later in 2011 he reprised his role as James Lester in the TV series ''[[Primeval (TV series)|Primeval]]''.<ref name="tv"/> From November 2011 he played the role of Louis Harvey in ''[[The Ladykillers (play)|The Ladykillers]]'' at the [[Gielgud Theatre]]. On 23 July 2012, Miller began touring for his book, ''It's Not Rocket Science,'' from the [[Royal Society]] in London. He also appeared at the [[British Comedy Awards]] with Armstrong on [[Channel 4]]. In 2013, Miller took part in an episode of ''[[Room 101 (British TV series)|Room 101]]'',<ref name="tv"/> and a ''[[Comic Relief]]'' special of game show ''[[Pointless]]''.<ref name="tv"/> On 13 December 2014, he appeared in a Christmas edition of ''[[The Chase (British game show)|The Celebrity Chase]]''.<ref name="tv"/>

From 2011 until the series three premiere in 2014, Miller starred in the [[BBC]]-French co-produced series ''[[Death in Paradise]]'' as Detective Inspector (DI) [[Richard Poole (character)|Richard Poole]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b01pvmf6/episodes/guide#b01pvmm2 |title=BBC One – Death in Paradise – Episode guide |work=BBC |date=1 January 1970 |access-date=4 December 2013}}</ref> A third series of ''Death in Paradise'' was commissioned for early 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.radiotimes.com/news/2013-02-12/death-in-paradise-series-three-confirmed |title=Death in Paradise series three confirmed |work=Radio Times|date=12 February 2013 |access-date=4 December 2013}}</ref> On 9 April 2013 it was announced that Miller would be departing the series, to be replaced by actor [[Kris Marshall]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Cole |first=Tom |url=http://www.radiotimes.com/news/2013-04-09/ben-miller-to-be-replaced-by-kris-marshall-on-death-in-paradise |title=Ben Miller to be replaced by Kris Marshall on Death in Paradise |work=[[Radio Times]] |date=9 April 2013 |access-date=4 December 2013}}</ref>

Miller explained he had personal reasons for the change: "It was the job of a lifetime, but logistically I just didn't feel I could continue. My personal circumstances just made it too complicated, but I will miss it like a lung. I love it here."<ref name=RTDIPMillerleaving>{{cite news|title=Ben Miller: Death in Paradise is the best job in TV|url=http://www.radiotimes.com/news/2014-01-14/ben-miller-death-in-paradise-is-the-best-job-in-tv|access-date=17 February 2014|newspaper=Radio Times|date=14 January 2014|author=Alexia Skinitis}}</ref> Miller's wife had discovered she was pregnant after he had begun filming the first series. Their time apart caused strains on his relationship with her and their sons, so he wanted to spend more time with his family.<ref name=RTDIPMillerleaving />

In 2014, Miller appeared in the feature film ''[[Molly Moon and the Incredible Book of Hypnotism]]''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Mitchell |first=Wendy |url=http://www.screendaily.com/news/production/rowleys-molly-moon-starts-shooting-in-london/5048211.article |title= owley's Molly Moon starts shooting in London | News | Screen |publisher=Screendaily.com |date=25 October 2012 |access-date=4 December 2013}}</ref> He also appeared with [[Billy Connolly]] and [[David Tennant]] in the film ''[[What We Did on Our Holiday]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.comedy.co.uk/news/story/00000115/cast_what_we_did_on_our_holiday_connolly_tennant/ |title=Parkinson joins comedy sexism debate |publisher=[[British Comedy Guide]] |date=21 July 2009 |access-date=2 March 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160109122814/http://www.comedy.co.uk/news/story/00000115/cast_what_we_did_on_our_holiday_connolly_tennant/ |archive-date=9 January 2016}}</ref> Miller guest starred in ''[[Doctor Who]]'' as the [[Sheriff of Nottingham]] in the third episode: "[[Robot of Sherwood]]".<ref>{{cite web |date=20 August 2014 |title=Details on Series 8′s First Four Episodes |url=http://www.doctorwhotv.co.uk/details-on-series-8s-first-four-episodes-65657.htm |access-date=29 August 2014 |website=Doctor Who TV}}</ref><ref name="Fact file">{{cite web |title=Robot of Sherwood: Fact File |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/articles/3ZHQ1xQCC6QYTDgX0fvCDBs/robot-of-sherwood-fact-file |access-date=7 September 2014 |website=Doctor Who |publisher=[[BBC One]]}}</ref>

Starring opposite [[Nancy Carroll (British actress)|Nancy Carroll]] and [[Diana Vickers]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://playbill.com/news/article/182147-Political-Comedy-The-Duck-House-Will-Play-Londons-Vaudeville-Cast-Announced |title=Political Comedy The Duck House Will Play London's Vaudeville; Cast Announced |publisher=[[Playbill]] |work=playbill.com |date=16 September 2013 |access-date=20 September 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130925153332/http://playbill.com/news/article/182147-Political-Comedy-The-Duck-House-Will-Play-Londons-Vaudeville-Cast-Announced |archive-date=25 September 2013 }}</ref> Miller played Robert Houston in the play ''[[The Duck House]]'' by [[Dan Patterson]] and Colin Swash.<ref name="Duck">{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-24108600 | title=The Duck House: MPs' expenses satire heads for West End | work=BBC News| date=16 September 2013 | access-date=16 September 2013}}</ref> The show is a political satire based on the [[UK parliamentary expenses scandal]].<ref name = "Duck"/>

In 2015, following the 800th anniversary of the ''[[Magna Carta]]'', Miller starred as [[John, King of England|King John]] in Series 6 of ''[[Horrible Histories (2015 TV series)#Series 6 .282015.29|Horrible Histories]]''.<ref name="tv"/>

In October 2015, Miller along with [[Ruth Jones (actress)|Ruth Jones]] and Will Close, appeared in adverts for British supermarket [[Tesco]] as Roger with Jones as his wife Jo and Close as their son Freddie. In 2016, Miller co-presented alongside [[Rachel Riley]] and [[Romesh Ranganathan]], the [[ITV (TV network)|ITV]] entertainment series ''[[It's Not Rocket Science (TV series)|It's Not Rocket Science]]''.<ref name="tv"/>

In February 2016 Miller issued a book, accompanied by a lecture tour, entitled ''The Aliens are Coming!'', examining the question "[[are we alone in the universe?]]"<ref>{{cite web|title=HLF - The Aliens Are Coming! With comedian Ben Miller|website=Huddersfield Literature Festival 2016|publisher=Lawrence Batley Theatre|url=http://www.thelbt.org/HLF-Aliens-Are-Coming-comedian-Ben-Miller|access-date=6 February 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160206192754/http://www.thelbt.org/HLF-Aliens-Are-Coming-comedian-Ben-Miller|archive-date=6 February 2016}}</ref> That year, Miller played the role of Murray in the six-part [[BBC]] sitcom ''[[I Want My Wife Back]]'',<ref name="tv"/> starring alongside [[Caroline Catz]]. In 2016 he appeared in the [[Channel 4]] comedy ''[[Ballot Monkeys]]''.<ref name="tv"/>

In 2018 he returned to the role of 'Bough', sidekick again to Rowan Atkinson's title character, in the film ''[[Johnny English Strikes Again]]''. In September of that same year he played the role of Wolf Hall on the BBC sitcom ''[[Upstart Crow]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/tv-radio/article/mark-rylance-ridiculed-by-upstarts-over-comedy-of-errors-23px93t5z|title=Mark Rylance ridiculed by upstarts over comedy of errors|last=Low|first=Valentine|date=11 September 2018|newspaper=[[The Times]]|access-date=6 August 2019|language=en|issn=0140-0460}}</ref>

In November 2022, Miller released his seventh children's book ''Secrets of a Christmas Elf''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://virginradio.co.uk/shows/82983/ben-miller-tells-chris-evans-why-his-new-christmas-book-will-get-kids-reading|title=Ben Miller tells Chris Evans why his new Christmas book will get kids reading|website=virginradio.co.uk|date=11 November 2022 |accessdate=6 December 2022}}</ref> In 2024, Miller acted as children's author Jullian Hartswood in the comedy drama ''[[Austin (TV series)|Austin]]'' for Australian television network [[ABC TV (Australian TV channel)|ABC TV]], and produced by [[Northern Pictures]] and Lincoln Pictures.<ref>{{Cite news |date=11 May 2024 |title=TV series filmed locally and starring big British stars gets air date |url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/8624718/filmed-in-canberra-austin-comedy-series-premiere-and-trailer/ |access-date=8 July 2024 |newspaper=The Canberra Times |publisher=Australian Community Media |location=Canberra |id={{ProQuest|3053584378}}}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Miller dated actress [[Rachel Weisz]] while they were both studying at [[Cambridge University]] during the early 1990s.<ref name="Thismuch" /> He married actress [[Belinda Stewart-Wilson]] in 2004, and they had a son before divorcing in 2011. He married production executive Jessica Parker, the daughter of musician [[Alan Parker (musician)|Alan Parker]], in September 2013; they have a son and daughter.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.yourlocalguardian.co.uk/leisure/comedy/10686986.TV_game_show_host_Alexander_Armstrong_was_best_man_at_comedy_partner___s_wedding/ |title=TV game show host Alexander Armstrong was best man at comedy partner's wedding (From Your Local Guardian) |publisher=Yourlocalguardian.co.uk |date=20 September 2013 |access-date=2 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2010/sep/11/ben-miller-family-values |location=London |newspaper=The Guardian |first=Caroline |last=Rees |title=Ben Miller: My family values |date=11 September 2010}}</ref> He has been diagnosed with [[obsessive–compulsive disorder]] (OCD).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Reilly |first1=Elaine |title='Professor T' star Ben Miller: 'I was born to play this part' |url=https://www.whattowatch.com/features/professor-t-star-ben-miller-i-was-born-to-play-this-part |website=WhatToWatch |date=5 August 2021 |access-date=10 April 2023}}</ref> Despite reports to the contrary, in an interview with [[Roman Kemp]] on [[BBC Radio 5 Live]] in December 2024, Miller said he could not play the drums and did not know where this claim came from.<ref name="HWM1" /><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/m0025trd| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20241207130319/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/m0025trd| url-status = dead| archive-date = 7 December 2024| title = Roman Kemp with Maddie Moate, Stephen Mangan and Ben Miller| author = Roman Kemp| website = BBC Sounds| date = 2024-12-07| access-date = 2024-12-07}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 2021, with the cast of ''[[Bridgerton]]'', Miller received a nomination for the [[Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nominations Announced for the 27th Annual Screen Actors Guild Awards |url=https://www.sagawards.org/media/news/releases/nominations-announced-27th-annual-screen-actors-guild-awards |website=Screen Actors Guild Awards |publisher=Screen Actors Guild |access-date=4 February 2021 |date=4 February 2021}}</ref>

In 2025, Miller was nominated for a [[Logie Awards of 2025|Logie award]].<ref>{{cite news |work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]] |access-date=11 August 2025 |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-08-03/the-2025-logie-award-winners-live-blog/105603414 |first1=Caitling |last1=Rawling |last2=Winter |first2=Velvet |first3=Hannah |last3=Story |url-status=live |archive-date=4 August 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250804031828/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-08-03/the-2025-logie-award-winners-live-blog/105603414 |title=Logies 2025: Lynne McGranger wins Gold Logie, Fisk sweeps up comedy awards — as it happened |at=SILVER LOGIE — Best Lead Actor in a Comedy |date=3 August 2025}}</ref>
